items.title: 67259_Big Chief Moore oral history interview
items.q: I always loved to hear either Jack Teagarden or a, or a -- any of the big bands or big name musicians

ctx.x: Very beautiful. That's -- I'm sure that a song like that and a -- and a kind of a melody and the flavor that that melody has has appeared in some of your work as you became a professional musician. Would you feel -- do you feel that some of that a, that feeling and that melody has come up in things that you've played over the years in various orchestras when you've been playing with people like Buster Bailey and Henry "Red" Allen?

Oh yes, yes, yes, yes. I learned the art of projection -- to project to the listeners in the audience by watching the great musicians that I have worked with. As you say Buster Bailey and "Red" Allen and Louis Armstrong and many, many greats that I can't a -- I could mention, I mean in the short space of time like we -- like here. I have worked with many. I've learned how to, how to get that rhythm and also the blues and sing things like "Basin Street", "Saint James Infirmary". And some on my albums are -- are on…

you learn a few things from somebody that is unknown. You'd be surprised how many I've listened to that I have never heard name mentioned before, and you know who they are. I go to a club; I listen, and I get things like that.
